blocks.text: Origin / creation. Researchers from philosophy, cognitive science, history, ecology, language, and prediction formed an institution to compare internal variation with transformation produced by encounters across boundaries.
Identity / human status. Artificial research and civic institution. It did not discover a measurable mystical substance.
Importance. The Observatory clarified that num concerns expansion of reachable becoming, not randomness, intensity, surprise, or simple novelty. It contributed to the Proof of Recurrence.
Decline or corruption. Civic dependence on its measurements encouraged institutions to optimize for apparent num. Its research authority expanded into administrative and market power.

Final status / surviving function. Absorbed into recurrence auditing and the Bureaucracy of Num. Its final definition survives in Reduction doctrine, while its institutional history warns that measuring openness can narrow it.
